title: SBI for experimental evolution learning assessment

pre.title: What does each evolutionary force do?
pre.prompt: Match each biological force to its main role in the simulator.

post.title: Reconnect force and consequence
post.prompt: The labels changed, but the biological roles did not. Match them again.

targets.label: Makes replicate paths differ by chance

knowledge_questions.feedback: Mutation supplies variants, selection changes their expected reproductive contribution, and finite-population sampling produces drift.

pre.title: Build one generation
pre.prompt: Arrange one simulator generation using the convention used in this workshop.

post.title: Advance the population once
post.prompt: Rebuild the workshop’s one-generation convention from its operations.

cards.label: Move probability into newly formed states

knowledge_questions.feedback: This workshop advances each generation as mutation, then selection, then drift; changing that convention can change a discrete-time model.

pre.title: Now run the logic backwards
pre.prompt: You observed an evolutionary trajectory. How can simulations help you learn what generated it?

cards.label: Parameters θ drawn from plausible values

post.title: Trace evidence back to mechanism
post.prompt: Place the parallel pieces that connect a measured frequency history to plausible biological causes.

cards.label: Learn which simulations resemble the data

knowledge_questions.feedback: Candidate parameters generate simulated data. SBI compares those simulations with the observation and returns uncertainty over plausible parameters.

pre.title: Several explanations fit
pre.prompt: Three different parameter combinations explain the measured trajectory almost equally well. What should we conclude?

choices.label: Pick the parameter set whose curve looks best.
Keep uncertainty over the plausible parameter combinations.

post.title: One dataset, several mechanisms
post.prompt: Separated parameter regions produce trajectories consistent with these sparse observations. What should the inference retain?

choices.label: Only the region with the narrowest-looking curve.
One midpoint between all parameter regions.
Probability across the distinct plausible regions.

knowledge_questions.feedback: When several parameter combinations are consistent with the data, the posterior should preserve that uncertainty instead of forcing one answer.

pre.title: Build rejection ABC
pre.prompt: Put the simulation recipe in order.

cards.label: Keep parameters whose simulations are close

post.title: Reconstruct the ABC filter
post.prompt: Arrange the same logic using a new description of each operation.

cards.label: Sample a candidate from scientific prior knowledge
Measure discrepancy from the real trajectory

knowledge_questions.feedback: Rejection ABC draws from the prior, simulates, compares with the observation, and retains parameters from sufficiently close simulations.

pre.title: Design the observation
pre.prompt: You can afford one additional measurement. Where would you put it?

post.title: Place one informative sample
post.prompt: A new set of mechanisms agrees at first and diverges later. Where is one added sample most informative?

knowledge_questions.feedback: Measure where competing hypotheses predict the largest separation. That location can change with the hypotheses being compared.

confidence_questions.statement: I can turn a biological hypothesis about evolution into a stochastic simulator.
I can reason from an observed trajectory to uncertainty about the evolutionary processes or parameters that generated it.

post_evaluation_questions.statement: This workshop changed how I think about connecting mechanistic models with experimental data.
I can imagine using at least one idea from this workshop in my own research.
